claims.statement: Directory structure constrains URL routes, but directory names do not perfectly mirror navigation labels; for example, /src/langsmith/fleet/ maps to 'No-code agents' in the navigation UI.

Most authored OSS content is emitted as separate Python and TypeScript route trees: /src/oss/python/ and /src/oss/javascript/ are included only in their matching output, while shared OSS directories such as /src/oss/langchain/, /src/oss/langgraph/, and /src/oss/deepagents/ are built for both languages with conditional fences resolved per target.

Files named managed-deep-agents*.mdx in /src/langsmith/ generate language-prefixed routes (/langsmith/python/managed-deep-agents-... and /langsmith/javascript/managed-deep-agents-...) appearing in the Build tab Managed Deep Agents, with unversioned URLs redirecting to the Python routes.

The AGENT DEVELOPMENT LIFECYCLE product has five menu items: Home, Build, Test, Deploy, Monitor. Build contains two language dropdowns (Python, TypeScript), each with 10 tabs. Test, Deploy, and Monitor contain flat tabs with no language split.
Test, Deploy, and Monitor menu items draw from files flat in /src/langsmith/ organized by functional topic without directory structure constraints.

OpenWiki and Deep Agents Code are the two OSS exceptions to language duplication: /src/oss/openwiki/ builds once at /oss/openwiki/... and /src/oss/deepagents/code/ builds once at /oss/deepagents/code/..., both using the Python conditional-content branch.

For each target language, the builder preprocesses MDX, rewrites versioned snippet imports, rewrites unqualified OSS links unless they are already language-qualified or belong to an unversioned OSS product, and rewrites unversioned Managed Deep Agents links to the target-language route.

Builder tests assert the key route boundaries: language-prefix rewriting, one-time unversioned OSS output, dual Managed Deep Agents routes, language-scoped snippet imports, and source-symlink exclusion.

The PRODUCTS AND SETUP navigation has five menu items: LangSmith setup, LLM Gateway, No-code agents, Engine, and Deep Agents Code. LangSmith setup alone is tabbed, with Overview, Account, Cloud, BYOC, Self-hosted, and Govern.

Deep Agents Code is an unversioned Products and setup surface whose expanded Configuration group is rooted at oss/deepagents/code/configuration and contains credentials, config file, hooks, and MCP tools; the configuration landing page documents distinct precedence for general options, provider keys, dotenv files, and provider endpoints.

Engine is a flat src/langsmith/engine*.mdx Products and setup surface whose direct navigation pages cover overview, issue workflow, GitHub integration, issue categories, webhooks, security, and self-hosted operation.

Deep Agents Code captures DEEPAGENTS_HOME before dotenv loading, preventing a project dotenv from relocating the trusted profile root; its configuration commands report effective settings and origins without printing secret values.
The builder rejects source-tree symlinks and files resolving outside the collection root, preventing a committed source path from bringing host files into build artifacts.

The Managed Deep Agents Build tab has Get started, Agent capabilities, and Build and deploy groups for both Python and TypeScript routes, and its project-structure page is an authored language-fenced source whose required root agent export and managed-path conventions resolve per language.

BYOC separates LangChain cloud control-plane responsibilities from sensitive customer-AWS data-plane resources; onboarding uses a cross-account IAM role and moves a data plane from Requested through Provisioning to Active, while workspaces are permanently associated with the selected data plane.
The LangSmith setup Self-hosted tab configures direct /langsmith/self-host... routes and marks the SmithDB group hidden, while placing its metrics route in the visible Reference group.

The Deploy Sandboxes tab configures direct LangSmith sandbox routes for the landing page, snapshots, service URLs, download links, auth proxy, mounts, permissions, CLI, SDK, and Harbor integrations; the landing page also directs self-hosted setup to the deployment guide.

The Monitor Overview tab places the `langsmith/observability` landing page separately from the Trace, Debug, Observe, and Reference tabs; the landing page links tracing setup, trace investigation, dashboards and alerts, automations, feedback, and Engine.

The shared Deep Agents subagents source is emitted to both language route trees and placed in the Delegation group; it describes synchronous delegation as blocking the coordinator until completion, while no synchronous subagents removes the task tool and asynchronous subagents use a separate mechanism.

Engine runs a closed issue loop: it detects recurring trace issues, diagnoses against traces and connected source code, proposes a pull request, tracks matching traces and dataset examples, and reopens an issue that resurfaces.

The Playground model-provider reference is a direct LangSmith route under Deploy → Prompt & Context Hub → Prompts; it documents provider-specific configuration and authentication, including Bedrock trusted-entity and self-hosted Azure workload-identity paths.

Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor tracing guides are placed in Monitor → Trace → Tracing setup → Integrations → Developer tools, while the SDK secret-redaction guide is placed in the Trace tab's Data & privacy group.

The Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor tracing integrations redact known secrets locally before upload by default; this redaction does not cover unrecognized credential formats, and Cursor attachments bypass it entirely unless attachments are disabled.

The Monitor Reference LangSmith REST API group instructs Mintlify to generate `langsmith/smith-api` pages from the committed platform OpenAPI specification; a daily workflow fetches and post-processes the live specification, hiding internal and Fleet operations and grouping public tags for readable reference navigation.

The Self-hosted tab's visible Reference group places the RSS-enabled self-hosted changelog alongside release-version documentation; each changelog entry identifies the Helm chart version, packaged LangSmith version, release channel, and download artifact.
